## Summary

Pocock's takeaways from watching poteto's talk: (1) **"Lock down your agents"** — humans like 'sharp knife' abstractions that are powerful but cut you if used wrong; Lauren's finding is that agents perform much better in extremely [truncated — by context, constrained/locked-down environments]. The quoted tweet is the talk itself: "here's how i shipped 2,500 PRs last month to production" — free on X video, watch on 2x.

## Why it matters

- **Constraint-as-capability lands on a cluster we already hold.** Locking down agents = fewer sharp knives = the same thesis as [[2026-09-14-rauchg-verifiers-skills-new-frameworks]] (verifiers/skills over frameworks) and [[2026-09-17-agrawal-agent-simplification-prompts]] (rules where rules suffice): narrow permissions and small blast radius beat general power. A practitioner shipping 2.5k PRs/month is the strongest production datapoint yet for that thesis.
- **Cross-links the same-week Pocock cluster.** The /fix-one-thing idea ([[2026-10-01-pocock-fix-one-thing-skill]]) is a locked-down agent by design: one standards violation, small PR, small blast radius. And the review-throughput thesis of [[2026-09-26-pocock-retro-pr-talk]] presumes exactly this kind of constrained generation.
- **Skepticism gates:** talk unwatched at capture; takeaway #1 is truncated mid-definition ("extremely…"); 2,500 PRs/month is a throughput number for one org with unknown review depth — cargo-culting the rate without the gates would be slop at scale.
